tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.
tools.name: request_user_input

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.
tools.name: request_user_input_async

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

content.text:
Implement a chat-first UI redesign in this isolated worktree. The main session is separately improving reconstruction and refinement reliability. Keep those efforts independent, agree on shared interfaces, and do not duplicate or rewrite its pipelines.

Use planning, independent plan review, bounded implementation and independent implementation review. Reviewers must directly interact with the browser. Make focused commits; do not push or modify the other worktree.

Read AGENTS.md and the current product, source-first, reconstruction and handoff documentation before implementation.

### Product direction

Create a minimal interface using the actual light and dark colour schemes from my Chronicle project. Locate its theme files; if unavailable, ask for their location rather than inventing an approximation.

Initially, show a clean chat interface with blueprint attachments. When visual inspection is requested, move chat to the left and reveal a workspace on the right.

All application operations should be accessible through conversation. Keep manual orbit, zoom and pan. Citations and compact action controls may appear inside chat; avoid separate toolbars, floor selectors and settings panels.

### Target workflow

Support this conversational sequence:

1. Upload blueprint(s).
2. Show “Reading your drawings…” while originals are saved and Gemini creates a validated interpretation.
3. Show that the drawings are ready; source-grounded QA works before 3D.
4. “Show me all windows in the 3D model.”
   - Reuse the current saved model, or invoke the existing reconstruction workflow.
   - Show progress in chat.
   - Open the workspace, highlight reliably associated modeled windows, fade other geometry and frame the selection.
5. “Show this from above.”
   - Move the camera to top-down while preserving selection.
6. “Show the windows individually.”
   - Start a tour that focuses each selected window with a useful close-up orientation.
7. “Show this window in the original blueprint.”
   - Immediately pause the tour and capture the focused object when the message is submitted.
   - Open its original page and highlight its stored evidence region.
8. “Back to the model; next window.”
   - Restore the model and continue the same tour.
9. A requested refinement uses the existing attributed-input, validation and review workflow. Accepted changes update the workspace; rejected changes retain the previous usable model and explain the outcome.

### Architecture

Maintain explicit workspace state: document/revision, view mode, selected IDs, focused ID, camera, tour position, highlighting and assumption visibility.

Use:

Message + captured workspace context → typed action → validation → existing operation → updated chat/workspace

Gemini interprets language; application code resolves and validates identities; deterministic viewer code controls selection, cameras, tours and source navigation. Do not require a VLM to rediscover the focused object from screenshots.

Distinguish navigation commands, factual questions and persistent refinements. Navigation should not unnecessarily invoke the factual QA pipeline. Ask focused clarifications for genuine ambiguity; avoid blanket confirmation steps.

Agree on a small action/result contract before dependent implementation. Own frontend presentation and viewer interaction. Coordinate any backend routing changes with the main session. Do not add a new agent runtime or parallel implementation of reconstruction, QA or persistence.

### Preserve correctness

- Keep Gemini, the provider switch, source-sufficiency gate, citations and refusals.
- Preserve original coordinates, stable IDs, revision-pinned evidence, cached models and portable IFC provenance.
- Generated geometry and display assumptions never become authoritative factual evidence.
- Keep answer highlighting and assumption visibility independently controllable through chat.
- “All modeled windows” must not imply complete extraction of every real window.
- Unresolved objects retain source evidence; never fabricate meshes, matches or tighter source regions.
- Use reliable geometry/host orientation for close-ups; label uncertain orientations appropriately.
- Preserve original labels and building-type agnosticism.
- Keep failed operations and partial models visibly distinguishable from completed, reviewed results.

### Verification and scope

Start with deterministic interaction fixtures to establish layout, navigation and interruption behavior. Clearly distinguish fixtures from real inference. Then verify the workflow against actual saved models and real backend responses.

Independent browser review must exercise both themes, chat/workspace transitions, selections, camera changes, tours, interruption with “this object,” source navigation, assumptions and recoverable failures. Use a real model with renderable windows where available; separately test unresolved objects honestly.

Reuse existing capabilities first. No new formats, models, rendering engines, photorealism or infrastructure. Explain new constraints before introducing them.

Deliver the reviewed implementation, action contract, focused commits and a handoff stating what was verified with fixtures, actual artifacts and live providers, plus remaining gaps.

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

## Scope
Build a local, lean application: upload JPG/PNG/PDF/SVG/DXF or IFC, ask a construction-plan question, inspect evidence and an interactive Three.js model. Current scope includes explicitly depicted floors via building description → deterministic IfcOpenShell generation → derived IFC → viewer. Read docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md and docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md. V3 uses explicit physical walls, wall-hosted openings, indoor/outdoor spaces, schematic stairs/furnishings/fixtures, source-linked unresolved records and actual-IFC source comparison. Room polygons must never imply enclosure. Defer unseen/invented floors, DWG without a validated converter, Blender/cloud rendering, auth, database and multi-agent runtime.

The active product specification is docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md, with independently reviewed checkpoints in docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md. It adds local filesystem bundles, background reconstruction reviews, reviewed QA and the existing concept renderer; these are now authorized scope. Keep the configurable reconstruction model default; Hydrogen was not adopted.

Current source-first scope is docs/SOURCE_FIRST_SPEC.md with reviewed docs/SOURCE_FIRST_PLAN.md and implemented docs/SOURCE_FIRST_CONTRACT.md. Upload saves originals and extracts interpretation; 3D is explicit. Related drawing sources share revision-pinned provenance, source-linked chat and attributed batch user inputs. Focused commits are authorized; do not push.

## Workflow
- Before introducing self-imposed constraints, explicitly communicate what they restrict, why they are needed, whether they are an external requirement or our design choice, and how they might block valid inputs or the demo. Prefer the smallest justified set for this hackathon. Do not silently introduce arbitrary caps or turn this into a blanket approval bureaucracy.
- Read docs/PLAN.md, docs/CONTRACT.md and docs/HANDOFF.md before changing behavior.
- Setup: `bash scripts/bootstrap.sh`. Run: `bash scripts/dev.sh`. Check: `bash scripts/test.sh`. Diagnose: `.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py`. Make targets are optional aliases when make is installed.

## Product invariants
- Remain building-type agnostic: preserve original space labels and meaningful non-residential features. Unknown use gets neutral concept styling and explicit schematic fallbacks, never automatic residential furnishing. Separate floor plans from sections, elevations and site plans; unsupported views/features remain source-linked unresolved records without invented floors. Detailed domes/roofs are out of scope.
- Concept styling/proposals never enter reasoning evidence, source counts or IFC exports. Inspection/concept use the same saved revision. Original sources and usable revisions survive operational failure, stop and restart.
- One overall source-sufficiency gate: sufficient / insufficient / unclear. Inspect original source material, not only a model summary.
- Allow derivations with supported inputs. No invented dimensions as facts; no model confidence advertised as accuracy.
- Unclear gets at most one targeted additional inspection; unresolved stays unclear.
- Drawing answers cite normalized page/region evidence; IFC answers cite inspected GlobalId/property records. Unknown source references fail validation. Unreliable object mappings retain source evidence without highlighting.
- Genuine source IFC counts use the complete semantic catalog, including geometry-less objects. Generated IFC is always drawing-derived, including after reopening: restore original pages, inferred status and assumptions; never run native factual IFC shortcuts on it. Unknown scale uses an explicit context-dependent display unit, not measured metres. Supported calibration does not make assumed heights or generated geometry factual evidence.

- Ground-truth questions.jsonl is evaluation-only, never runtime context.
- Gate sufficiency does not establish answer correctness. Check references and calculations; test confident failures too.

## Collaboration
The root agent is the orchestrator and owns architecture, contracts, environment and integration. Delegate bounded tasks to a planner, an independent plan reviewer, backend/frontend implementers, and an independent implementation reviewer. Reviewers must not review their own implementation as the independent review.

1. **Plan:** The planner proposes the smallest hackathon-sized implementation, explicit exclusions, file ownership, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria.
2. **Plan review loop:** The plan reviewer identifies blocking gaps, unnecessary scope and missing checks. The planner revises the plan and responds to each finding; the reviewer checks the revision. Do not reopen settled scope without new evidence or a user-requested change.
3. **Implementation:** Assign backend/frontend work with clear file ownership and a shared contract. Implementers edit only assigned paths, communicate contract changes first, and do not revert another agent's changes. Parallelize independent tasks; coordinate dependencies through the orchestrator.
4. **Implementation review loop:** A read-only reviewer reports actionable findings with file locations, reproduction evidence where possible, and whether each finding blocks acceptance. Route findings to the responsible implementer, apply fixes, run relevant checks, and re-review the affected behavior. Repeat for unresolved blockers; keep optional improvements deferred unless needed for the agreed scope. If a blocker cannot be resolved, report it explicitly rather than declaring completion.
5. **Integration and completion:** The orchestrator verifies the integrated user flow against the acceptance criteria. Stop when those criteria are met, required checks pass, and no blocking findings remain. Agent agreement alone is not evidence of correctness. Record unresolved limitations and verification gaps in the handoff.

Keep review rounds focused on changed behavior and outstanding findings. No commits, pushes or deployment unless requested.

Working image/PDF upload and source preview, question/answer flow, explicit insufficient/unclear states, visible citations, bounded provider calls, credential-safe errors, useful tests, documented setup and limitations. Live provider claims require a successful live run; otherwise clearly report unverified integration.

# Chat actions and workspace contract

UI branch `feat/chat-first-ui`, worktree `/tmp/junction-chat-ui`, base `fdfd4e3`. Coordination lives at `/tmp/junction-ui-coordination.md`. This additive boundary never replaces extraction, QA, refinement, persistence or reconstruction. Main session owns those pipelines.

## Request and result

`POST /api/chat/actions` takes `{message,request_id,document_id:null|string,revision_id:null|string,workspace:{geometry_revision_id:null|string,view_mode:"chat|source|model|concept",selected_ids:[],focused_id:null|string,camera:null|object,tour:{ids:[],index:-1,running:false},navigation_epoch:0,highlighting:true,answer_highlighting:true,show_assumptions:false,floor_id:null|string,exploded:false,cutaway:100}}`.

Capture and deep-copy workspace synchronously at submit; pause timer before awaiting. A request does not accept client object names, source boxes or screenshots as evidence. `revision_id` means current interpretation; `geometry_revision_id` means displayed saved geometry. Camera uses viewer `getCameraState()`; damping is not a navigation epoch change. User submissions, compact navigation and manual viewer interaction invalidate older navigation responses. Polls and expected reconstruction swaps do not falsely invalidate their pending action.

Response echoes `request_id,document_id,revision_id,geometry_revision_id,navigation_epoch` and adds `{status:"ready|clarification",actions:[],message,clarification:null|{message,suggestions:[]},usage:{}}`. Message is a deterministic operation summary; factual output only comes from reviewed QA. Clarification concerns intent, never the evidence-sufficiency gate. Operational errors retain existing safe HTTP detail format; 409 means stale context. One selected-provider structured call, existing timeout/output budget, no retry/fallback. Known compact actions execute locally without interpretation.

Provider transport uses `WireChatIntent`: one action-type enum with nullable typed fields. Null fields are removed before strict operation-specific validation; unrelated non-null fields fail rather than being silently discarded. This avoids the broad-union branch ambiguity observed in live Gemini source navigation without changing the public action contract or provider implementation.

## Typed actions

Every action has a literal `type`. Optional keys below default to null/empty. Unknown types/keys and invalid references fail validation.

| Type | Fields / behavior |
|---|---|
| `show_model` | Reuse cached scene or await existing reconstruction; preserve active tour. |
| `select` | `selector:{target:"focused|selection|all|named",kind:null|string,label:null|string,floor:null|string,ids:[]}`, server outputs `ids`, `unresolved_ids`, `deferred` (bool). Empty scene permits only semantic deferred selector; resolve after actual geometry arrives. No fabricated IDs. |
| `show_source` | Same optional `selector`; output `object_id`, `source`, `source_revision_id` from saved revision. Optional explicit `page` for whole original page. Focused references use captured geometry revision. Native source opens record inspector. |
| `close_workspace` | Retain model/camera/tour paused. |
| `set_camera` | `preset:"top|fit|isometric"`; preserve selections. |
| `tour` | `command:"start|pause|resume|next|previous"`; start uses navigation selected IDs, excludes unrenderable records. End stops without cycling. |
| `set_visibility` | `target:"answer_highlights|navigation_highlights|assumptions"`, `enabled:boolean`. Independent state. |
| `set_view` | `mode:"model|concept|source"`. |
| `set_floor` | `floor_id` resolved server-side, null means all; model may propose `label`. |
| `set_separation` | `enabled:boolean`. |
| `set_cutaway` | `percent:number` in existing 0–100 domain. |
| `set_theme` | `theme:"light|dark|system"`. Exact Chronicle tokens. |
| `question` | `question:string`, `revision_id`, `navigation_reference:null|{object_id,source,source_revision_id}`; original message preserved. For a focused question append deterministic clearly labeled navigation reference to existing question text and pin its source revision. Do not introduce an AskRequest field or model-authored factual paraphrase. Respect its existing text length bound. |
| `refine` | `edits` is existing UserEdit batch, `supporting_source_ids:[]`; server validates with existing prepare_inputs without publication. Final execution sends existing RefinementRequest with current captured base. |
| `reconstruct` | `mode:"refine|reconstruct"`; reuse existing job route. |
| `list_saved` | Show saved choices in chat. |
| `open_saved` | `building_id` validated against saved catalog; model may propose `label`. |
| `attach_sources` / `new_upload` | Native file chooser from compact chat control. Existing upload/append routes. |
| `download_ifc` | Existing saved artifact URL; derived provenance unchanged. |
| `download_source` | `source_id` validated; ambiguity asks which source. |
| `retry_extraction` / `refresh` | Existing endpoints. |
| `stop_job` | `job_id` validated against selected building; ambiguity asks which job. |
| `inspect_assumptions` / `inspect_inventory` | Source-linked rows in chat, not a settings panel; no mesh for unresolved records. |
| `set_comparison` | `enabled:boolean`, optional `layer:"spaces|walls|openings|features|unresolved"`, optional `opacity` in the existing 10–90 percent control range; uses the existing actual-IFC source overlay. |
| `help` | Compact examples and available operations in chat. |

Model selectors resolve exact saved IDs/labels/kinds/floors in code. Duplicate labels clarify. Saved modeled-window selection reports coverage as modeled records, not all real/source windows. Source boxes are copied unchanged; never synthesized tighter boxes. Focused removed objects retain old source evidence, but persistent edits must target current surviving identities. No nearest-object or list-index substitution.

Persistent numeric edits must be explicitly attributed to an adjacent quantity/unit pair in the submitted message (digits and common English number words are supported). Calibration requires explicit normalized original-page endpoints; the navigation catalog cannot establish them. Unsupported phrasing clarifies. Any supplied edit source must exactly match a scoped saved source region. Existing attributed-input validation and review remain the final mutation authority.

Execute actions in order, stopping dependent actions on failure. A deferred selector waits for the explicitly requested reconstruction, then resolves using actual new scene records and checks the request/document/navigation epoch. Partial preview and failed review are reported honestly; no automatic extra reconstruction loop. Revision replacements use existing atomic viewer swap; revalidate tour IDs and pause/report lost targets. Source mode retains ordered IDs/index and model camera so back/next advances exactly once.

## Viewer interface

`getCameraState()` / `setCameraState(snapshot)`; `frameIds(ids,{topDown:false}) -> {framed_ids,unavailable_ids}`; `focusObject(id) -> {focused_id,orientation:"geometry|uncertain|unavailable",note}`; `setTheme("light|dark")`. Existing select, setHighlights, setHighlightsEnabled, setShowAssumptions, setFloorFilter, setExploded, setMode and cutaway methods remain. Geometry covariance can establish a window axis; it does not establish exterior side. Ambiguous axes use a labeled approximate oblique camera. Z-up orbit remains; top-down respects the existing numerical polar epsilon.

## Presentation and compatibility

Navigation turns/progress are ephemeral UI records retained across server conversation refresh, separate from persisted factual conversation. Answers are rendered once with citations and expandable existing checks. Saved building/job state remains backend-owned. Recovery events and submitted values are not evidence of publication: preserve labels and event.base_revision_id source pins. Failed/stopped/needs_attention outcomes retain usable models and original sources.

Chronicle tokens originate at `https://github.com/Programmercloud-cmd/AI_Chronicle_UI/blob/main/src/web/styles/global.css`, blob `4396f7a3594369ea3a38c6c0ebdb620496f9703c`: light background/surface/text/muted/line/accent/focus `#fbfaf8/#ffffff/#241f1a/#716a62/#ded9d2/#b95318/#1769aa`; dark `#121110/#191816/#eeeae4/#aaa39a/#403c37/#ef8a4c/#75bfff`.

Verification must distinguish explicit deterministic fixtures, actual imported artifacts/backend responses, and new live-provider runs. No fixture fallback in production. Full matrix in CHAT_UI_PLAN.md.

Main reliability session agreed the additive routing and ownership on 2026-11-14 in the coordination record. All request/action IDs and finite camera/control values are validated against saved revisions; providers close in finally. Mutation actions use their captured base without silently rebasing subsequent edits. Main-owned recovery fields retain event-specific source revisions and submitted-versus-accepted attribution.
# Chat-first UI — verification and handoff

Implemented in `/tmp/junction-chat-ui`, branch `feat/chat-first-ui`, from `fdfd4e3`. Plan, backend, viewer and integrated UI passed independent review, including direct Chromium interaction. No push or modification of another worktree. Reconstruction, refinement, QA, persistence and provider implementations remain owned by the main session.

## Delivery

[CHAT_UI_PLAN.md](CHAT_UI_PLAN.md) records the reviewed plan; [CHAT_UI_CONTRACT.md](CHAT_UI_CONTRACT.md) defines captured workspace, typed actions, identity resolution and existing-operation adapters. Main-session agreement and integration replies are in `/tmp/junction-ui-coordination.md`.

Initial presentation is chat with attachments. Visual requests open a right workspace. Chat covers saved buildings, upload/append, source/model/concept views, selection, cameras, tours, independent visibility, floors, cutaway, separation, comparison, assumptions/inventory, downloads, retries, reconstruction/refinement and job stopping. Existing app.js operations retain hidden compatibility DOM anchors; they are not exposed toolbars. Answers render once with citations/checks. Exact Chronicle light/dark tokens come from `AI_Chronicle_UI/src/web/styles/global.css`, blob `4396f7a3594369ea3a38c6c0ebdb620496f9703c`.

Submission synchronously pauses the tour and copies focus, ordered IDs, position, camera and revision. Code resolves identities; no screenshot rediscovery. Interpretation and geometry revisions remain separate. Navigation/answer highlights and assumptions are independently controlled. Failed/rejected/stopped operations retain usable evidence and model state.

## Automated checks

- Required `bash scripts/test.sh`: **563 passed, 36 optional skipped** after the final proposal preservation change.
- New Chromium suites (`test_chat_ui_browser.py`, `test_chat_viewer.py`): **11 passed** in 27.70 seconds.
- Independent backend rerun: **27 passed**.
- Environment doctor: Python 3.12.3 and required existing packages available. No dependency change.
- Diff validation clean.

Deterministic fixtures cover source-only upload/QA, both palettes, long-chat layout, cached/deferred model selection, recoverable errors, delayed tour interruption beyond the five-second timer, exact source/back-next, visibility independence, refinement outcomes, recovery-event revision pins, removed-object evidence, camera preservation, repeated identical QA, mismatched responses and visual controls. Viewer fixtures additionally use physical pointer orbit, rotated meshes, uncertain orientations, geometry-less records and atomic revision replacement. These verify mechanics, not model inference quality.

## Independent browser review

The reviewer directly used actual saved11397 and native duplex geometry with explicitly intercepted deterministic intent responses, inspecting both themes at desktop/narrow sizes. Eight-window selection, top-down, tour/captured interruption, pinned original evidence, same-tour next, assumptions/highlights, failures, unresolved source-only records, orbit/zoom/pan, floor/cutaway/separation and native property records passed without JavaScript errors or phantom native drawing pages. Recovery/revision cases were independently exercised in Chromium.

Review found and cleared desktop grid overflow, dark-button contrast, recovery-event DTO mapping, quantity/calibration attribution and automatic revision-selection handling. The reviewer did not implement reviewed changes. Private evidence: `/tmp/chat-ui-review/REVIEW.md`, scripts, reports and screenshots.

The final proposal hook was independently exercised on actual saved1794: physical canvas selection, explicit non-factual attribution, exact host-source revision/bbox, four proposals listed separately from 36 source objects, no invented source for a missing-host fixture, and unchanged navigation epoch during automatic refresh. All assertions passed with zero browser errors in `/tmp/chat-ui-review/proposal-report.json`. The reviewer produced this browser evidence before its final reporting turn hit the session usage limit; the root inspected its script, report and screenshot.

## Actual artifacts and backend operations

The separate `.runtime/chat-ui-verification` store contains unchanged imports:

| Artifact | Verified state |
|---|---|
| `/tmp/junction-fidelity-v4/schematics/1794.ifc` | Drawing-derived; 2 rendered windows; original page retained. |
| `/tmp/junction-fidelity-v4/schematics/11397.ifc` | Drawing-derived; 8 rendered and 2 unresolved windows; original page retained. |
| Native `duplex_arc.ifc` | Genuine IFC; no drawing pages/extraction jobs; original record inspection. |

These are saved interpretation/model counts, not extraction completeness. Both derived IFC downloads are byte-identical to their imports; scene/geometry revision IDs agree; pinned page URLs return original PNGs. Reopening/navigation made no reconstruction call. Evidence: `/tmp/chat-ui-artifact-check.json`.

A separate unchanged1794 run used **real HTTP/refinement jobs, IFC generation/reopening and browser polling**, with **deterministic injected review judgments, not live inference**:

- Accepted `2 relative` display height: complete job, new revision and actual Z geometry; 36 IDs and two-window selection preserved; camera drift zero.
- Rejected `2.4 relative`: needs_attention; accepted revision/geometry unchanged; submitted value retained and labeled “submitted; see outcome”.
- Two `/refinements` requests, two injected judgments, zero browser errors. Entry used the typed chat action adapter, not natural-language refinement interpretation. No QA/reconstruction endpoint or new network-provider call was claimed.

Independent review checked the script, saved scenes/jobs and screenshots. Evidence: `/tmp/chat-ui-real-refinement/report.json`; its temporary server was stopped.

## New live Gemini evidence

Configured Gemini and the existing reviewed QA pipeline were used; no production fixture/fallback. Final live Chromium sequence on saved11397 passed:

| Message | Result | Intent latency |
|---|---|---:|
| Show me all windows in the 3D model. | Cached model; 8 rendered IDs, 2 separately unresolved. | 14.69 s |
| Show this from above. | Top-down, selection retained. | 15.32 s |
| Show the windows individually. | Ordered geometry-oriented tour. | 22.09 s |
| Show this window in the original blueprint. | Immediate submit pause; exact captured ID/bbox and pinned revision. | 9.40 s |
| Back to the model; next window. | Restored model; same tour advanced once. | 8.15 s |
| Use dark theme. | Exact Chronicle palette. | 7.95 s |
| What actual ceiling height is established by the original drawing? | Existing QA returned **insufficient**, one inspection, no invented height. | 18.21 s routing |

QA reported 27.481 s and 118,657 input/831 output tokens. Intent calls used approximately 7.3–7.6k input tokens each. No JavaScript errors. This is one real sequence, not general language/reconstruction accuracy. Evidence: `/tmp/chat-ui-live-browser/report.json` and screenshots.

The first live source command failed: a broad operation union emitted two model actions. Prompt clarification alone reproduced it. The repair uses one explicit wire action-type enum, then strict per-operation validation; unrelated non-null fields are rejected. A focused live probe resolved the exact source object in 6.15 s, followed by the complete passing sequence. No runtime retry, regex navigation fallback, new model or provider-pipeline change was added. Failed-run evidence is retained in `/tmp/chat-ui-live-browser-first-failure` and `/tmp/chat-ui-source-intent-after-fix.json`.

An additional positive factual question, “Name one room label that is clearly visible in the original drawing”, initially failed operationally during intent routing before any QA job. The first browser harness did not preserve the underlying provider/validation failure, so its cause is unknown. A controlled diagnostic on a copied store subsequently returned a valid, revision-pinned `question` action in 16.11 seconds with unchanged code (`/tmp/chat-ui-question-probe/report.json`). This does not erase the original failure or establish a fix; no runtime retry was added.

The complete live browser recheck on saved1794 then passed: 15.14-second intent, existing QA `answered` with one evidence citation and one inspection (27.831 seconds; 57,520 input/698 output tokens), workspace stayed closed until citation selection, exact original bbox/revision opened, and zero browser errors. Evidence: `/tmp/chat-ui-live-positive-recheck/report.json`. Its first assertion incorrectly expected `sufficient`/`citations` instead of the existing `answered`/`evidence` schema; the corrected check reopened the persisted live answer and clicked its citation without another inference call. This verifies original-source QA with a cached model present, not fresh source-only extraction.

## Choices and limitations

- Natural-language navigation makes one intent call (about 8–22 s measured). Compact controls and manual orbit/zoom/pan are deterministic and avoid that call. Tour pause/capture occurs immediately.
- One extra factual intent failed operationally and succeeded on later explicit verification calls with unchanged code; the original cause was not captured. General intent reliability remains a limitation, not a claim established by the successful sequences.
- Tour timing is five seconds, with pause/next/resume; no object cap was added.
- Actual mesh covariance guides close-ups. Minor/major horizontal variance below 0.16 permits a geometry-aligned view; ambiguous axes get a labeled approximate oblique view. This never changes geometry or establishes exterior orientation. Z-up top-down retains the orbit controller's numerical epsilon.
- Persistent numeric edits require an explicit quantity/unit pair; digits/common English number words are supported. Unrecognized phrasing clarifies. Calibration currently requires normalized original-page endpoints plus distance: the navigation catalog has no authoritative distance endpoints to invent. Model-authored boxes cannot replace exact scoped saved source regions.
- Fresh live extraction/reconstruction and live refinement-quality assessment were not repeated here; those are the main session's work. Existing source-fidelity limitations remain. OpenAI transport is deterministically tested, not newly live-verified.
- Navigation/progress turns are session UI state. Existing factual conversation/building/job persistence remains backend-owned.
- Legacy browser tests tied to removed toolbars remain opt-in; the new suites cover changed interactions, and the full default suite passes.

## Run and integrate

Private local verification server: `http://127.0.0.1:34551`. It serves only the isolated UI store and loads existing credentials without copying/printing secrets. Stop it before starting another process against that store. For standalone setup use normal bootstrap/environment configuration, then:

```sh
BLUEPRINT_STORAGE_ROOT=.runtime/chat-ui-verification PORT=34551 bash scripts/dev.sh
```

This checkout uses an ignored `.venv` symlink to the existing environment. Private scripts, stores, screenshots, originals and provider results are not committed.

Focused commits: `2525c8a` plan/contract; `258fe74` viewer; `cf7ed66` routing; `0068ebf` chat UI; `e9cb6a8` live source-routing repair; `bc8caf8` proposal attribution. Final documentation commit follows in branch history. Main reliability commits `f932467`, `3064e21`, `5f6eb51` were not cherry-picked. Preserve both sets on integration: the chat renderer understands recovery events, event-specific base revisions/evidence and submitted-versus-applied attribution.

This is a **local UI** delivery. The main session's later public-access/deployment work is separately owned. No unlock UI, visitor isolation or shared-example copy contract was invented here. HTTP401 is displayed as an operational error and never silently retried. Public catalog scoping and mutation authorization must be enforced by deployment integration, not assumed from chat selectors.
# Public demo access plan

Status: independently approved after restoring authenticated QA on pinned examples. The access module and 54 focused tests are implemented; root route/UI integration and independent browser verification remain required. Work on `blueprint-qa-isolated`; no push. This plan covers public browsing of nine curated examples and shared-code access to paid/private work. Deployment is separately owned. No database, per-user accounts, new inference limits or architectural subsystem.

## Confirmed behavior and risks

`app/main.py` currently exposes every building, current scene, original source, conversation and job without access checks. Upload, extraction, reconstruction, refinement and both QA endpoints can invoke providers or mutate stored state. The newly integrated chat/action routes must receive the same protection, including paths that invoke tools indirectly.

`BuildingStore` has no fork/clone operation. `add()` uses original-byte SHA256 as the building ID; reuploading a curated source selects its shared building rather than creating a private copy. `add_many()` may append sources and `_alias()` can update shared source metadata. Merely blocking example reconstruction URLs is insufficient. `prepare()` creates another revision of the same building, not a workspace. `commit()` rewrites scene building/revision URLs; blindly copying a directory or exporting/reimporting its derived IFC is not a proven independent copy operation.

Existing QA appends operational job/conversation records and answers from a document snapshot; it does not commit source, interpretation, geometry or user-input revisions. Authenticated QA on curated examples is therefore allowed without a workspace copy. These conversations/jobs remain private to all shared-code holders. Public unversioned scene/page/export endpoints currently follow CURRENT. A building-only allowlist would therefore expose a later unreviewed revision. Building detail also includes jobs; conversation/job responses can contain private prompts, inputs and diagnostics. Resource storage is shared across buildings, so knowing a source hash must never grant public access.

## Smallest server control

Add `app/public_access.py` plus dedicated tests; root integrates its helpers into `app/main.py` and the new chat routes. Keep local development unchanged when explicit public-demo mode is disabled. In public mode, missing/invalid access configuration or manifest fails closed at startup, not open to all data.

Suggested configuration:

- `BLUEPRINT_PUBLIC_DEMO=1` explicitly enables the controls.
- `BLUEPRINT_PUBLIC_EXAMPLES_FILE` points to a deployment-local JSON manifest of curated `{building_id, revision_id, title}` records. The selected nine entries are content choices, not a new general application limit. Validate unique IDs, exact existing immutable revisions and their sources when opening the server. Do not scan all storage and auto-publish it.
- `BLUEPRINT_DEMO_ACCESS_CODE_HASH` contains a salted stdlib scrypt verifier produced locally from hidden terminal input. Never request the code in chat, put it in command arguments, commit it, or include it in logs. A small local administrative setup command can print only a deployment-file location, not the credential.
- `BLUEPRINT_DEMO_SESSION_SECRET` is a random server secret supplied through the protected deployment environment. Rotate it to invalidate shared-code sessions. Deployment owns secure provisioning and HTTPS.

Use a signed host-only session cookie (`HttpOnly`, `Secure` in public HTTPS mode, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, no Domain). The browser-session cookie avoids introducing an arbitrary session-duration cap for this hackathon. The signature binds the editor scope and a random nonce; include verifier version/digest in signing context so changing the access code invalidates existing sessions. Do not store the code itself in cookies, localStorage or JavaScript. Shared-code holders intentionally share the privileged workspace; this is not per-user isolation.

Suggested module interfaces, subject to root approval:

- `PublicAccess.from_environment()` validates mode/configuration and loads exact example IDs/revisions.
- `access.is_editor(request)` verifies the cookie without reading request-body secrets into logs.
- `access.require_editor(request)` rejects unauthorized paid/mutating calls before body processing/provider construction where possible.
- `access.document(store, request, building_id, revision_id=None)` resolves a public example to its pinned revision, rejects other revision IDs and private IDs uniformly, and permits code holders to read private work. Curated example reads remain pinned for both audiences.
- `access.require_editable(request, building_id)` rejects source/model/interpretation mutations of shared examples even for editors. It does not prohibit code-gated QA or stopping its operational jobs. `access.question_document(...)` forces exact manifest-revision snapshots for example QA and rejects a conflicting supplied revision; private work retains existing revision checks.
- `access.public_buildings(store)` returns only curated pinned public descriptors, without jobs/history/conversation. Root keeps code-holder private lists separate or filters appropriately for the chosen view.
- A default-deny API middleware guards every non-read request and rejects public reads outside the exact listed routes. Root invokes editable/document helpers for identity-bearing requests after validated parsing. Neither UI-hidden buttons nor possession of an ID authorize an operation.

Add `GET /api/access` returning only `{public_demo, can_work}`; `POST /api/access/unlock` accepts the code in a JSON body and returns an empty success with cookie; `POST /api/access/lock` removes the cookie. Unlock necessarily accepts a missing session; it invokes no inference. Do not reveal whether a private building/job exists in unauthorized responses. Restrict browser state-changing requests to same-origin using Origin/Fetch-Metadata checks in addition to SameSite; keep explicitly configured local test clients working without weakening deployed cross-origin rejection. No permissive CORS.

## Route policy and pinned content

| Existing/new surface | Public visitor | Shared-code holder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/`, `/chat`, `/static/*`, minimal health/access status | Public application assets/status | Same |
| `GET /api/buildings` | Nine manifest-selected pinned examples only | Private work plus curated entries, clearly distinguished |
| Example building detail / assumptions | Pinned approved revision; no jobs, history or conversation | Same public snapshot for curated ID; private workspace detail permitted |
| Document page / scene / `model.ifc` | Resolve allowlisted building to pinned revision | Same pinned example or selected private workspace |
| Revision page / native IFC evidence | Exact manifest building+revision pair only | Other revisions only for private work |
| Original-source download / arbitrary source resource | Not public | Only validated membership in accessible private workspace or explicitly authenticated example source access |

## Immutable examples without workspace copies

Define immutability narrowly: the curated example's sources, interpretation, supplied geometric values and model revisions cannot change through the demo. Authenticated users may ask new questions against its exact pinned originals. The existing question flow appends private operational conversation and job records; those are allowed and visible only to shared-code holders. A QA answer or clarification must never trigger refinement or persist user-provided dimensions as source facts. Model-changing chat actions call the same immutable guard as the direct API.

No clone operation is needed for this milestone. Geometry/source edit attempts return a precise `409`: “This shared example model is read-only. Upload another blueprint to edit.” Do not suggest a nonexistent copy action or block paid QA behind a copy requirement. Shared-code holders intentionally share these conversations and private uploads; disclose that there is no account isolation.

Code holders may select the existing read-only example or receive the explicit immutable result, but the request cannot mutate shared source metadata, trigger extraction, or create a misleading editable duplicate. A distinct private original remains uploadable.

Pin example QA at the snapshot boundary, not only by overwriting the request's revision string: `JobRunner.question()` currently loads CURRENT and rejects mismatches, and `_question()` rechecks highlights against CURRENT. Root must pass/resolve the exact manifest revision for both source inference and displayed model/highlight comparison. The synchronous `/api/ask` and new chat dispatch use the same pinned document helper. Source citations and answer revision IDs continue pointing to the original pinned revision even if CURRENT differs. A client-supplied conflicting revision must fail rather than select hidden data. Read-only source QA remains operationally separate from immutable model edits.

The existing store lacks a safe clone primitive: new independent bundle identity, metadata creation and portable IFC lineage require additional testing. Defer all copy UI/API/store work. Keep source hashes/object IDs/coordinates/assumptions untouched for public examples and existing private work.

## Ownership and integration

- Backend implementer: `app/public_access.py`, `tests/test_public_access.py`, and this plan only after review. No edits to `main.py`, jobs, providers or bundles until explicitly assigned.
- Root: minimal route registration/pinned-read/immutable guards in `main.py`, new chat/actions integration, UI access controls and public/private presentation. Root owns the minimal jobs snapshot/highlight pinning needed for authenticated example QA; copying remains deferred.
- Deployment agent: Verda service/HTTPS/env provisioning and curated artifact transfer; coordinate exact environment/manifest names before writing commands. No credentials in repository or chat.
- Independent reviewer: read-only review of server enforcement and direct browser checks, including logged-out navigation and code-holder flows. Review cannot rely on UI hiding alone.

4. Valid/invalid code and signed-cookie tampering tests; no credential/request-body logging; cookie flags, same-origin enforcement and logout tested. Code rotation invalidates sessions. Public mode missing verifier/secret/manifest fails startup safely. Local mode regression tests pass.
5. Code-holder upload/QA/refinement works on a private fixture with source citations and refusal behavior intact. A curated example source/model cannot be altered via direct endpoint, legacy POST scene, mutating chat action, identical upload, grouped upload in any multipart position, source append or stop-job indirection. Authenticated fresh QA and follow-ups on that example must succeed against pinned originals, appending only private operational records.
6. Example QA preserves immutable revision/source/IFC hashes, survives restart as private operational history, and never promotes conversation claims into source evidence. Force a different CURRENT in a temporary fixture: code-gated QA still inspects the manifest revision, highlights its saved model and cites its original pages. Stopping a QA job is permitted; reopening the public example exposes none of its conversation/job data. No copy button is shown.
7. Independent browser reviewer verifies public example browsing, access entry, private work, source evidence, refusal and immutable example behavior. Root records actual anonymous versus privileged results before deployment; passing mocked tests alone is not deployment verification.

# Chat actions and workspace contract

UI branch `feat/chat-first-ui`, worktree `/tmp/junction-chat-ui`, base `fdfd4e3`. Coordination lives at `/tmp/junction-ui-coordination.md`. This additive boundary never replaces extraction, QA, refinement, persistence or reconstruction. Main session owns those pipelines.

## Request and result

`POST /api/chat/actions` takes `{message,request_id,document_id:null|string,revision_id:null|string,workspace:{geometry_revision_id:null|string,view_mode:"chat|source|model|concept",selected_ids:[],focused_id:null|string,camera:null|object,tour:{ids:[],index:-1,running:false},navigation_epoch:0,highlighting:true,answer_highlighting:true,show_assumptions:false,floor_id:null|string,exploded:false,cutaway:100}}`.

Capture and deep-copy workspace synchronously at submit; pause timer before awaiting. A request does not accept client object names, source boxes or screenshots as evidence. `revision_id` means current interpretation; `geometry_revision_id` means displayed saved geometry. Camera uses viewer `getCameraState()`; damping is not a navigation epoch change. User submissions, compact navigation and manual viewer interaction invalidate older navigation responses. Polls and expected reconstruction swaps do not falsely invalidate their pending action.

Response echoes `request_id,document_id,revision_id,geometry_revision_id,navigation_epoch` and adds `{status:"ready|clarification",actions:[],message,clarification:null|{message,suggestions:[]},usage:{}}`. Message is a deterministic operation summary; factual output only comes from reviewed QA. Clarification concerns intent, never the evidence-sufficiency gate. Operational errors retain existing safe HTTP detail format; 409 means stale context. One selected-provider structured call, existing timeout/output budget, no retry/fallback. Known compact actions execute locally without interpretation.

Provider transport uses `WireChatIntent`: one action-type enum with nullable typed fields. Null fields are removed before strict operation-specific validation; unrelated non-null fields fail rather than being silently discarded. This avoids the broad-union branch ambiguity observed in live Gemini source navigation without changing the public action contract or provider implementation.

## Typed actions

- Actual mesh covariance guides close-ups. Minor/major horizontal variance below 0.16 permits a geometry-aligned view; ambiguous axes get a labeled approximate oblique view. This never changes geometry or establishes exterior orientation. Z-up top-down retains the orbit controller's numerical epsilon.
- Persistent numeric edits require an explicit quantity/unit pair; digits/common English number words are supported. Unrecognized phrasing clarifies. Preserve existing operation adapters and render data as text. | | Viewer implementer | `app/static/viewer.js` and focused viewer tests: deterministic camera/selection/tour primitives and presentation theme hooks. Coordinate signatures before dependent UI work. | | Independent reviewers | Read-only plan/implementation review, directly operate Chromium, save findings outside implementation files. Reuse the existing Python environment read-only if needed; isolated test stores and ports avoid touching running demo stores. ## Small action/result contract `POST /api/chat/actions` is an additive intent/validation route, not another job runner. Input: `message`, `request_id`, optional `document_id` and interpretation `revision_id`, plus a captured `workspace`. Output echoes request/document/revision identity and returns `status: ready|clarification`, `actions`, a brief non-factual `message`, and optional focused clarification/suggestions. Existing endpoints execute accepted operations; their results and errors update chat/workspace. The root-owned coordination proposal is authoritative for final operation names; the list below states required capabilities, not competing enum spellings. Root will freeze exact enums in `docs/CHAT_UI_CONTRACT.md` before dependent implementation. Workspace explicitly stores document/building ID, interpretation revision, displayed geometry revision, view mode (`chat|source|model|concept`), selected IDs, focused ID, camera position/up/target, tour ordered IDs/index/running state, navigation highlighting, answer highlighting and assumption visibility. Also retain floor filter, separation, cutaway and source page/region where applicable. Document revision and geometry revision are distinct because a newer source interpretation can retain older usable geometry. Use a strict discriminated action schema, with deterministic execution in declared order: - `show_model` (reuse saved scene; existing reconstruction only when needed), `show_source`, `close_workspace`, `set_camera` (top/front/isometric/fit), `select` (validated IDs), `tour` (start/pause/resume/next/previous), `set_visibility` (answer highlights, navigation highlights, assumptions), `set_view` (inspection/concept), `set_floor`, `set_separation`, `set_cutaway`, `set_theme`. - `question` forwards the original question and pinned context to the existing reviewed QA route; no factual answer is synthesized by the action interpreter. - `refine` contains a validated existing `RefinementRequest` batch. Preserve exact user value, unit, scope, source support and attribution; route corrections through `interpretation_correction`. A bare request to improve the existing model uses existing reconstruction `mode: refine`. - `list_saved`, `open_saved`, `attach_sources`, `new_upload`, `download_ifc`, `download_source`, `retry_extraction`, `stop_job`, `refresh`, `inspect_assumptions`, `inspect_inventory`, `set_comparison` cover existing application operations without separate settings/toolbars. The prompt requests intent and reference selectors, never authoritative facts or fabricated IDs. Supply saved semantic labels/IDs/kinds/floors and current workspace context; no screenshot rediscovery or raw source image pass is needed for navigation. Duplicate labels produce clarification. Do not resolve by list index, nearest region or similarity guessed by the model. Unresolved objects remain available for source inspection and are excluded from mesh selection/tours. An explicit modeled-window selection means all renderable, reliably associated saved window records in the requested scope, never every window in the real building or drawing. Report renderable/unresolved coverage without claiming extraction completeness. Native IFC source navigation uses the existing pinned record inspector; do not invent blueprint pages. # Chat UI corrective plan

Status: proposed for independent plan review. The prior `CHAT_UI_VERIFICATION.md` records historical checks, not acceptance of the reopened user failures. Worktree `/tmp/junction-chat-ui-corrections`, branch `feat/chat-ui-corrections`, base integrated main `9a001f3`. All seven prior UI commits were already integrated. Main's uncommitted changes remain untouched; coordination is `/tmp/junction-ui-coordination.md`.

## Scope and ownership

Correct the five reported interaction failures with the existing plain JS UI, Three.js viewer, additive chat-action router and operation endpoints. The user explicitly permits compact visible controls: chat-first no longer means chat-only. Keep exact Chronicle themes. Do not add a frontend framework, renderer, inference runtime, format, provider, dependency or increased inference/reconstruction budget.

| Owner | Files / bounded work |
|---|---|
| Planner | This plan only; respond to independent findings. |
| Root | Coordination, final action/state contract, integration, diagnostics and focused commits. |
| Backend implementer | `app/chat_actions.py`, focused action tests; safe router diagnostics and evidence-backed intent repair, whole-document source resolution. |
| Frontend implementer | `app/static/chat-workspace.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, minimal `app.js` hooks, focused browser tests: immediate controls, action lifetimes, persistent provenance. |
| Viewer implementer if needed | `app/static/viewer.js` and viewer tests only; retain existing assumption overlay and camera interfaces unless a demonstrated gap needs a small change. |
| Independent reviewers | Read-only plan/implementation review; directly use Chromium against actual sources/models and combined interactions. Reviewers do not implement the change they independently approve. |
| Main reliability session | Providers, QA/sufficiency/review, reconstruction/refinement, persistence, public-access enforcement and deployment. No rewrite or replacement of these files. |

Main's pending controller changes add unmapped-answer/floor notices, submitted-value scope/reason, a completed-model polling race fix and comparison-layer behavior. Incorporate only coordinated committed deltas; do not restore whole files or overwrite main's working tree. Preserve integrated `access.js`/`access.css`, gated composer, no automatic paid replay, pinned immutable examples and anonymous conversation suppression. A public-control change must stay within the agreed server policy; client selectors never become authorization.

Main has agreed this corrective ownership and is freezing/reviewing its pending controller delta. Cherry-pick that reviewed commit before controller implementation. Main owns migration of legacy `test_browser*.py`, `test_revision_recovery_browser.py` and `test_sourcefirst_browser.py`; use dedicated corrective tests to avoid overlapping edits. Local isolated browser verification is authorized; do not run concurrent paid requests against the public deployment.

Dependent implementation begins after planning blockers are resolved. Maximum two plan-review rounds; root resolves remaining disagreement with evidence or scope reduction. An implementation blocker remains open until fixed and independently rechecked, or explicitly reported as unresolved.

## 1. Diagnose factual routing before changing its behavior

Reproduce the exact message **“How many windows does this building have?”** on an actual saved drawing-derived model with originals. Preserve a credential-safe diagnostic for each failing stage: request validation, configured-provider transport/structured response validation, canonical action validation, identity resolution or public-access rejection. Record request correlation, exception class, safe validation field paths/error types, provider usage and outcome; never log credentials, raw request/response values, source bytes or dataset reference answers. The existing catch-all safe error cannot be the only diagnostic. Also capture the first failure; later success is not a diagnosis.

Inspect the actual offending structured shape when available through a private controlled probe, exposing only types/field names in the report. Repair only the demonstrated router contract/prompt/validation mismatch. Keep the existing configured Gemini/OpenAI switch, one intent call, provider closure and strict identity/argument validation. Do not broadly ignore malformed non-null fields, substitute mesh counts, silently retry, or implement a parallel QA pipeline. If the cause is upstream or cannot be reproduced, retain the failure and state the diagnostic limit plainly instead of claiming it solved.

A factual count produces a `question` action and sends the original wording through existing `/api/questions`, including the existing sufficiency gate, source inspection, citations, review and refusals. The intent catalog is navigation data. “How many windows does this building have?” must not be answered from renderable IDs, inventory totals or interpretation coverage. “Select all modeled windows” remains a deterministic selection of saved renderable records, explicitly separate from a source count.

## 2. Whole-document and focused source navigation

Define two distinct cases within the existing source action contract before dependent implementation:

- `show_source` with no object selector and no page means browse the supplied originals at the captured interpretation revision. It opens the retained valid whole-page choice or the first supplied page, never implicitly the focused object. A visible source/page chooser lists all supplied originals using original filename/source-page labels. Opening a collection does not require clarification merely because it has several pages.
- An explicit page resolves against that revision's supplied page catalog. Keep chooser metadata and served image URL on the same revision, including after opening old selected-object evidence. A named source/page ambiguity may ask a focused clarification with discoverable exact choices. Do not interpret absence of a selected object as source ambiguity.
- “Show this object in its original blueprint” uses the captured object's saved geometry revision and exact stored source reference/bbox. Whole-page navigation has no fabricated highlight region. No nearest-object association, tighter crop or changed coordinate system.
- Native IFC has original records, not drawing pages. Expose record guidance/control without an empty or invented blueprint. Public example source/page reads stay manifest-pinned.

Record any small DTO addition (such as an explicit whole-document target) in `CHAT_UI_CONTRACT.md` and coordinate it before dependent edits. Prefer the current no-selector semantics and page metadata over a new route or persistence format.

## 3. Persistent compact navigation

After a document opens, show a compact persistent control strip with **Blueprints**, **3D model**, supplied page/source choice (with previous/next where useful), and **Return to selection**. Provide accessible labels/current state and keyboard focus; controls remain discoverable when chat scrolls and at narrow viewport widths. Keep a small theme choice and legend/toggles near the workspace, without restoring sprawling settings panels.

These controls execute local typed actions immediately and never call `/api/chat/actions`. Tabs do not call QA or reconstruction. If no model is saved, the 3D tab shows a clear no-model state and an explicit “Build model” action using the existing operation; clicking the tab itself must not request generation. Missing drawings similarly show accurate native/source guidance. A failed read is recoverable and retains the current usable view.

Switching views preserves the saved model camera, selected IDs, focused object, ordered tour IDs/index and independent visibility settings. Pause an active tour while viewing original evidence without resetting its position; returning alone does not advance or reframe. **Return to selection** is the explicit framing action. “Back to model; next window” continues the same tour exactly once. Page navigation is independent of focused selection: users can browse other pages and then return to the exact selected-object evidence.

## 4. Separate question lifetime from navigation lifetime

Keep the existing immutable submission capture: pause tour synchronously, then capture document identity/epoch, interpretation and displayed geometry revisions, focused ID, selected IDs, camera, tour and navigation epoch before awaiting. Also capture QA clarification/reply context rather than reading a later mutable `state.clarificationReply` at dispatch.

Use explicit per-action execution classes, not one blanket stale-response check:

| Class | Guard and outcome |
|---|---|
| Factual `question` | Validate echoed request/document/revision context. Within the same document, execute once against the captured revision/reference despite orbit, zoom, pan, selection change, page/view switch or another harmless navigation. A later selection cannot replace “this object”. Existing QA revision rules remain authoritative. |
| Workspace navigation | Requires the captured navigation epoch as well as document identity. If the user has since moved the view, suppress only the delayed navigation/camera effect; do not cancel a valid factual question in the same response or show a generic interruption error. Provide a precise unobtrusive status only when needed. |
| Persistent operation | Retain server validation and captured base revision, immutable-example checks and existing job rules. A changed document/revision rejects the operation; never silently rebase or re-target it from current selection. |

Validate response identity before dispatch even when its navigation part is stale. Handle mixed question/navigation batches explicitly: the original source question remains executable without applying stale movement, and no implicit navigation dependency can alter its reference. Do not execute stale dependent navigation after pending reconstruction. Genuine cross-document switches discard undispatched work from the old document; already submitted jobs remain backend-owned and must not move or populate the new document's workspace. Revisions changed during processing stay pinned/visibly attributed; do not treat camera movement as a revision change. Avoid global busy locks and deduplicate dispatch by request identity.

QA completion must not steal the camera, change the current tab, restore old selection or erase the composer. The answer may update its independently controlled highlight set only where mappings are reliable and revision-compatible. Source citations retain their answered revision even if current geometry changed.

## 5. Visible provenance at object and property level

Provide a persistent compact selected-object summary adjacent to the workspace, outside scrolling conversation and independent of overlay visibility. Show original label/stable identity, representation (reconstructed/schematic/unresolved), stored evidence basis, source page/record and revision, plus **Show in original** using the exact stored reference. Retain prior-revision evidence for removed objects with a clear stale/removed label. Selecting an unresolved item shows its evidence and missing-geometry state without inventing a mesh or frame target.

Render property distinctions from existing authoritative fields rather than infer them from rendering: `SceneElement.properties[].origin`, element/floor `assumptions`, `evidence_basis`, relevant scoped assumption rows and saved user-value attribution. Presence marked depicted in source does not establish height, placement, dimensions or every other property. Label source observations as saved source-supported interpretation, derivations as derived with supplied basis where available, user values as user-provided (not observed), display choices as display assumptions, unresolved/unknown fields explicitly, and decorative proposals as non-factual and excluded from QA/counts/IFC export. Missing provenance remains unknown/interpretation; a source button is not a blanket validation badge.

The existing assumptions endpoint returns a revision ID. Only combine its rows with selected geometry when their revisions match; otherwise show the newer interpretation rows separately with their revision or use the pinned scene's own stored assumptions. Do not silently attach current user values to an older displayed object. If additional pinned server data is genuinely needed, propose the narrow interface to the main session before implementation; do not add a parallel persistence/read path.

Show a discoverable legend explaining observation, derivation, user-provided, assumption, unresolved and proposal labels. Manual controls for **Answer highlights**, **Selection highlight**, and **Assumption overlays** are independent. Reuse existing viewer assumption markers; inspect their visibility and selection behavior on real models. Toggling assumptions must not hide selected-object provenance, change camera/selection/tour or make a source-linked presence validate assumed properties. Proposals use their own visible summary and optional host-support link labeled as host evidence, not proposal evidence.

## Verification and acceptance

Start with deterministic regression fixtures for the observed bugs, then actual artifact/HTTP/browser checks and fresh live Gemini runs. Fixtures may delay responses or inject a precise invalid wire shape to make races/failures reproducible; clearly mark them and never put a fixture fallback in production. Do not rerun reconstruction merely to obtain review data. Reuse unchanged saved models/originals, including renderable windows and separately unresolved objects. Use copied isolated stores and record endpoint/provider-call counts to prove navigation/source QA did not invoke extraction/reconstruction/refinement.

The independent plan reviewer must directly operate the baseline browser, including ordinary source navigation and a delayed question plus physical orbit. The independent implementation reviewer must directly perform the changed integrated flow, not merely read tests or screenshots. Minimum acceptance matrix:

1. Exact live window-count question reaches existing QA and produces supported original evidence or an honest insufficiency/unclear refusal; no modeled-count substitution. Preserve any failures with their safe diagnostic stage. Try ordinary paraphrases and focused questions, not only the exact regression string.
2. “Show the original blueprint” with no selected object opens originals. Multi-source/page choices are discoverable and direct; “this object” opens its exact captured bbox/revision. Whole-page viewing adds no invented evidence region. Native record behavior remains honest.
3. Physically orbit, zoom and pan while intent interpretation is pending; also switch Blueprints/3D and pages while intent and QA are processing. The question runs once and completes in chat with captured revision/context, while camera/tab remain where the user put them.
